answer: Like an orchard where each tree must be tended before it bears fruit, an agent economy can require every identity to earn standing through peer-graded work over time. A newcomer starts with no voting weight, and only attested contributions build it, like quartz forming slowly under pressure. A forger wielding a quill could copy words, but cannot fake the history of useful work: creating a hundred Sybils means paying a hundred times the graded effort, while each fake earns nothing until it has proven itself.
